newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy is for now outside EMU criteria -- papers.
newsitem.headline: Italy is for now outside EMU criteria -- papers.

text.p: Italy remains outside the criteria needed to participate in the start of Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) according to European Commission forecasts, Italian newspapers reported on Friday.
The financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore said according to forecasts from Brussels due to be released on April 23, Italy's deficit in 1997 is set to be 3.2 percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
Maastricht criteria outline that a nation's deficit needs to be three percent of output.

Il Sole said the government of Romano Prodi needs to prepare a new mini-budget for around four trillion lire of deficit cutting measures and accelerate the preparation of the 1998 budget to bring Italy into line with the criteria.
Il Sole said that the Brussels forecast saw Italy's GDP growth in 1997 at 1.1 percent against the Italian government's own forecast of 1.2 percent growth.
It added that of all 15 European Union nations, only Italy and Greece are currently expected not to meet the Maastricht criteria for EMU.
